strategies.name: London open breakout (Asian range breakout), classic
strategies.entry_rule: Define Asian range = high/low from 00:00 to 07:00 UTC (variants: 00:00-06:00 UTC, 23:00-06:00). After 07:00 UTC, enter long on first close (or stop order) above the range high; short on first close below the range low. One trade per day; cancel untriggered side once one fills. Backtrex implementation: H1 bars, breakout of Asian range after London open, 2016-10-02 to 2026-10-01.
strategies.exit_rule: Fixed SL/TP or close at a time cutoff (commonly 12:00 UTC or NY close) if neither is hit.
strategies.stop_loss_rule: Backtrex: fixed 35 pips. Common retail variants: opposite side of the Asian range, or range midpoint.
strategies.take_profit_rule: Backtrex: fixed 70 pips (2:1). Variants: 1x range height projected from breakout, or trailing.
strategies.claimed_performance: Backtrex (vendor backtest, EUR/USD H1, 2016-10-02 to 2026-10-01): 1,230 trades, 36.3% winners, profit factor 0.87, total return -28.0%, CAGR -3.2%, max drawdown -31.4%, only 3 of 11 calendar years positive (none by more than 2.5%); buy-and-hold +0.1%. Same vendor on GBP/USD M15: PF 0.72, total return -60.0%, CAGR -8.8% over 10 years.
strategies.notes: The most-cited intraday EUR/USD strategy and the clearest negative result found. Backtrex notes >100 trades/year makes costs decisive. A gold (XAUUSD) 3.7-year MQL5 study of the same idea exists but is not EUR/USD. Range window definitions differ by source; treat the window as a parameter to sweep.

strategies.name: Statistical London breakout (babypips thread variant)
strategies.entry_rule: Reconstruction of the long-running babypips 'Statistical London Breakout' thread: measure the range from 00:00 to 07:00 GMT (some posters use 02:00-07:00 ex-Sydney noise); place buy stop a few pips above the high and sell stop a few pips below the low at 07:00-08:00 GMT; skip the day if the Asian range exceeds ~50% of the 14-day ADR (breakout 'already happened').
strategies.exit_rule: Close at 12:00 GMT or when TP/SL is hit; cancel the other pending order on fill.
strategies.stop_loss_rule: Opposite side of the range or ~20-30 pips, whichever is smaller (thread varies).
strategies.notes: No verifiable aggregate statistics in the thread excerpts found; one poster reports avoiding EURUSD/EURGBP because they move before London open. Treat the range-width filter as the one idea worth testing on top of S01.

strategies.entry_rule: Reconstruction: measure the London-session move from 07:00 GMT to 12:30 GMT. If price is at/through a higher-timeframe level (prior day high/low, H4 swing) at the 12:30-13:30 GMT window and prints a rejection candle (pin bar/engulfing) on M15, enter against the London direction.

strategies.name: ICT Judas swing (London killzone sweep of the Asian range)
strategies.entry_rule: Killzone 02:00-05:00 ET (07:00-10:00 UTC). Price sweeps the Asian session high (low) by a few pips and closes back inside the range (M5/M15 close), ideally with a displacement candle and a fair value gap; enter short (long) on the retrace into the FVG/order block in the direction of the daily bias (prior-day direction or HTF structure).
strategies.exit_rule: Target the opposite side of the Asian range, then the prior day's low/high.

Another page claims London killzone forms the definitive daily high/low 58-64% of the time (unsourced).
strategies.notes: Vendor win rates (70%) conflict with the only large-sample test (gold, 50%). The daily-bias filter is the untested ingredient; both sources say unfiltered sweeps have no edge.

strategies.name: ICT Power of Three (accumulation-manipulation-distribution) daily model
strategies.entry_rule: Asian session (17:00-23:00 ET or 00:00-07:00 UTC) = accumulation range; London (02:00-05:00 ET) = manipulation (false move against the day's eventual direction); NY (07:00-10:00 ET) = distribution. Rule: after London sweeps one side of the Asian range and reverses back through the daily open, trade in the direction of the reversal, targeting expansion through the other side of the range during NY.
strategies.exit_rule: Close at NY lunch (12:00 ET) or at the opposite-side liquidity target.
strategies.take_profit_rule: Opposite side of Asian range, then prior day high/low.
strategies.claimed_performance: MQL5 blog test on 18 years of gold (not EUR/USD): unfiltered PO3/Judas patterns near 50% ('coin flip', 4,841 days); author suggests killzone, HTF direction and key-level filters. No EUR/USD statistics found.
strategies.notes: Equivalent to 'daily open mean reversion + continuation' framed as narrative; the testable statistic is: P(day's close is on the opposite side of the open from the London-session extreme). See fact F-18.

strategies.name: Asian session range fade (Tokyo mean reversion)
strategies.entry_rule: From 00:00 to 06:00 UTC (variants 22:00-02:00 UTC), after the range from 22:00 UTC is at least 15 pips but under 40 pips, sell at the range high / buy at the range low when price touches it with RSI(14, M5) > 70 / < 30, targeting the range midpoint.

strategies.name: 4pm London fix intraday pattern (USD rises into fixes, reverses after)
strategies.entry_rule: Krohn, Mueller & Whelan (J. Finance 2024, 5-min data 1999-2019, 9 G10 pairs incl. EUR): USD appreciates in the hours before the Tokyo, Frankfurt(ECB 14:15 CET) and London 16:00 fixes and depreciates afterwards (W-shaped 24h pattern). Strategy: short EUR/USD from ~13:00 London to 16:00 London; long EUR/USD from 16:00 London to ~20:00 London (reverse after fix).
strategies.exit_rule: Time-based: exit at the fix / 4 hours after.
strategies.stop_loss_rule: None in the academic version; practical 0.5 x ADR.
strategies.claimed_performance: Paper: 30-40% of daily volume executes in the 3 hours before and 1 hour after the London fix; pattern not driven by stale quotes; magnitudes are for a dollar portfolio, EUR/USD-specific pip sizes not extracted. The Full FX month-end case studies show 10-20 pip spikes/reversals within the 5-minute WM window on some month-ends and nothing on others.
strategies.notes: Best-documented intraday seasonality in FX. Returns are small per day and must beat spread; the paper attributes it to dealer hedging of client fix orders. Month-end amplifies it (S15).

strategies.name: Month-end fix flows (rebalancing into the last-business-day 16:00 London fix)
strategies.entry_rule: Reconstruction of sell-side practice: on the last business day of the month, estimate rebalancing direction from the month's relative equity performance (if US equities outperformed European equities in the month, foreign managers sell USD to rebalance -> expect EUR/USD bid into the 16:00 London fix, and vice versa). Enter 2-3 hours before the fix in that direction; exit at the fix; optionally fade after the fix.
strategies.exit_rule: Flat at 16:00 London; optional reverse position held to NY close.

strategies.name: Sunday/weekend gap fill
strategies.entry_rule: If the Sunday 22:00 UTC (Monday Asia) open differs from Friday's 21:00/22:00 UTC close by more than X pips, trade toward Friday's close (short a gap-up, long a gap-down). Filter by gap size relative to ATR.
strategies.exit_rule: Friday close (gap filled) or time stop Wednesday London (DailyForex finding).
strategies.stop_loss_rule: 1x gap size beyond the open (or 0.5 x ATR(14)).

ForexFactory post: EUR/USD gaps filled 66.15% (period unstated; GBP/USD 72.18% for 2002-2010). fxnx (500 Sunday opens, EUR/USD+GBP/USD+USD/JPY, methodology undisclosed): gaps < 0.50x daily ATR filled within 48h 88.4% (EUR/USD); gaps > 0.75x ATR filled within 24h only 28.2%, within the week 41.9%. EarnForex: average weekly gap ~70% of Friday's open-close range; no correlation between gap size and surrounding ranges. MQL5 forum anecdote: 98% of gaps over 18 months filled 'at some point'.
strategies.notes: Fill rates of 65-90% are consistent across sources but are mostly 'eventually filled' numbers; small gaps are also only a few pips, so after spread the edge is thin. Large (news) gaps fill much less often.

strategies.name: Pre-FOMC dollar drift (two days before the decision)
strategies.entry_rule: Karnaukh ('The Dollar Ahead of FOMC Target Rate Changes'): over the two days before a scheduled FOMC decision, the USD rises when fed funds futures imply a hike and falls when they imply a cut. Rule: if futures-implied change < 0 (cut expected) go long EUR/USD at the close two days before; if > 0 go short; exit at the 14:00 ET announcement.
strategies.claimed_performance: Macrosynergy summary of Karnaukh: USD -32 bp before expected cuts, +20 bp before expected hikes over the two-day window; stronger when FX implied vol is high; no rise in realised vol/illiquidity pre-FOMC. Mueller, Tahbaz-Salehi & Vedolin: USD excess returns significantly larger on FOMC days (pre- and post-announcement components), larger for high-rate-differential currencies. Borisenko & Pozdeev: the pre-decision drift is common to most currencies before their own central bank's cuts and 'the dollar drift ... averages to zero across specifications' (robustness contested). Lucca-Moench equity drift is not found for other macro releases.
strategies.notes: Eight events per year; the EUR/USD-only estimate is not isolated in the sources.

strategies.entry_rule: Forecast the monthly change in EUR/USD from the difference in Taylor-rule implied rates: i* - i = a + 1.5 x (pi_EA - pi_US) + 0.5 x (gap_EA - gap_US) [+ smoothing, real exchange rate term]; go long EUR when the model's predicted change > 0 (sign-based, monthly).
strategies.claimed_performance: Molodtsova & Papell (JIE 2009): short-horizon out-of-sample predictability for 11 of 12 USD pairs post-Bretton Woods, beating interest-rate, PPP and monetary models. Molodtsova, Nikolsko-Rzhevskyy & Papell ('Taylor rules and the euro', real-time 1999-2007): predictability only for specifications without the real exchange rate; persists through the crisis (2012). Ince, Molodtsova & Papell (2016, 1973-2014): strong evidence for Taylor-rule fundamentals vs random walk; Ince & Molodtsova real-time 15-country study: does not beat a random walk in some specifications.
strategies.notes: Statistical predictability (Clark-West tests) is not the same as tradeable Sharpe; monthly frequency.

strategies.name: Carry (EUR/USD interest differential) with time-of-day split
strategies.entry_rule: Hold the higher-yielding leg (short EUR/USD when US rates > EUR rates, as 2022-2025). Krohn-Mueller-Whelan: carry returns are earned intraday (US hours) and are ~zero overnight; momentum returns are earned overnight.
strategies.claimed_performance: Krohn et al. ('UIP in high frequency'): during the overnight period carry risk premia are essentially zero; the carry portfolio appreciates significantly during the day. No EUR/USD-only carry Sharpe retrieved; EUR/USD is a low-carry pair (differential ~2% in 2025).
strategies.notes: Implication for intraday systems: USD-positive drift during US hours when USD is the high-yielder.
